The decision requires neither proof of harm from every program nor flawless alternatives and does not make all media interchangeable. Facial vagueness and particular sanctions remain undecided.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Butler protects adults against confinement to children's material without prescribing hours. Pacifica and Red Lion are not overruled; Pacifica's three-Justice speech-value discussion is not made controlling.

##### The mandatory remedy and continuing nighttime protection

**Holding:** The appellate approval must be set aside, the corresponding FCC rule removed and §16(a)'s dependent command barred insofar as it requires the invalid 6 a.m.–10 p.m. schedule. The existing uniform 10 p.m.–6 a.m. protection and rejection of the favored-station distinction remain undisturbed.

**Proposition-level authority:** Ginsburg's Part III, joined by Stone-Zsela, O'Connor, Kennedy and Thomas, supplies five direct votes for final invalidity and mandatory removal; all nine preserve nighttime protection. Stone-Zsela calls the action on appellate approval vacatur and the other four reversal; their operative removal direction is identical. Souter does not join it.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The original §16(a) distinction covered public stations signing off at or before midnight from 6 a.m.–10 p.m., and other stations from 6 a.m.–midnight. The Government did not cross-petition to restore the harsher decree. Section 16(b)'s repeal of the all-day restriction remains. Section 551's conditional parental-choice provisions establish no presently effective technological alternative, repeal, mootness or automatic remand; no device-system factual premise is adopted. No replacement hour, station permission hearing, general new definition or automatic serious-merit defense is prescribed.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Remand through the D.C. Circuit for mandatory set-aside relief. Independently lawful FCC authority, §1464 and ordinary obscenity enforcement remain, but the invalid restriction cannot be reproduced under another label. No individual sanction, damages or later technology implementation is decided.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** X-Citement Video permits alternative defense of an existing judgment but not enlargement without the necessary petition. Chesapeake's actual-repeal remand does not follow from §551 alone. No Marks aggregation makes Souter's distinct validity-open remand controlling.

### Cable access and protected indecency

#### Denver Area Educational Telecommunications Consortium, Inc. v. FCC; Alliance for Community Media v. FCC, 518 U.S. 727 (1996)

**Docket or dockets:** Nos. 95-124 and 95-227.
**Decided:** June 28, 1996.

##### Whether 1992 §10(a)’s leased-access permission is facially invalid

**Authority of the judgment:** The facial challenge fails, 6–3: Stevens, O’Connor, Scalia, Souter, Thomas and Breyer sustain §10(a); Stone-Zsela, Kennedy and Ginsburg would invalidate it. No controlling sufficient rationale exists under Marks. Souter’s contextual accommodation rationale has Stevens, O’Connor and Breyer; Scalia and Thomas instead rely on the absence of a freestanding right to compel an unwilling private editor. Neither rationale is established as a logical subset of the other. The component judgment does not establish a general permission-review framework.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The retained permission allows, but does not require, prospective enforcement of a written and published policy prohibiting programming reasonably believed to depict or describe sexual/excretory activities or organs in a patently offensive manner under contemporary community standards, specified by the FCC for cable. Protected nonobscene indecency is included; this is not Miller’s full obscenity test and has no categorical serious literary, artistic, political or scientific value exemption, although context matters. No universal validation of indecency definitions, certification, actual policies or genuinely governmental facilities follows.

##### Whether §10(b)’s compulsory identification, segregation and opt-in arrangement violates the First Amendment

**Holding:** When covered leased-access programming is not voluntarily prohibited under §10(a), the government may not impose this integral identification/notification, channel-segregation, default-blocking and advance written-election system. Its cumulative burden on willing speakers and adult recipients fails independent necessity and means review despite compelling child-protection and parental-assistance interests.

**Proposition-level authority:** Souter’s Part III and V-B, joined by Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O’Connor, Kennedy, Ginsburg and Breyer; seven Justices.

**Material application:** Programmers identify and notify; operators concentrate covered speech on blocked capacity. Access requires a written request and FCC-required statement of adult age, fulfilled within thirty days, not a mandatory thirty-day wait; another blocked channel may be used if capacity is insufficient. The operator-installed lockbox accommodation described for systems without premium/pay-per-view channels leaves the operator holding the key/code pending a request and retains default denial and written opt-in. It differs from a household-controlled device. Mixed unpredictable programming creates real parental difficulty but does not justify the integral design’s delay, deterrence and channel-wide burdens. Household controls remain usable after opt-in.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No finding supplies a public registry, universal affordability, perfect technical alternative, implementation of 1996 blocking laws or absence of all supporting evidence. Ordinary age checks, notices, voluntary requests, subscription mechanisms and blocking devices are not individually held unconstitutional. No additional vagueness, prior-restraint or certification ruling is necessary.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Approval reversed, 7–2; the integral compulsory scheme and corresponding rules must be set aside, without a judicial replacement design.

##### Whether §10(c) may authorize suppression of protected indecency on PEG access capacity

**Authority of the judgment:** Approval is reversed within the protected nonobscene-indecency scope, 6–3: Stone-Zsela, Stevens, Kennedy, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer support relief; O’Connor, Scalia and Thomas oppose it. Souter/Stevens/Breyer’s contextual means/attribution ground and Kennedy/Stone-Zsela/Ginsburg’s strict legislative-content ground each have three votes. Neither is a demonstrated logical subset of the other; no controlling sufficient rationale exists under Marks, and no universal PEG public-forum or state-action rule is adopted.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Section 10(c) directs enabling rules concerning obscenity, sexually explicit conduct and unlawful-conduct solicitation/promotion; it does not compel operator censorship. The FCC interprets sexual explicitness through indecency and the unlawful-conduct category as otherwise proscribed material, permitting operator content certifications. Section (c) lacks (a)’s written/published-policy and reasonable-belief limits and (b)’s subscriber machinery. Lawful obscenity controls remain; unlawful solicitation and freestanding certification are not independently adjudicated, and protected advocacy is not automatically unlawful solicitation.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The corresponding rule must be set aside to the extent it authorizes protected-indecency suppression. This is final relief implementing the component judgment, not a remand to reconsider constitutionality after a universal franchise inquiry.

##### Whether §10(a) remains operative and what the judgment reaches

**Holding:** Section 10(a) remains independently operative after §10(b)’s removal. The permission’s independent operation and Congress’s purposes permit severance; the invalid compulsory scheme is removed as an integral whole.

**Proposition-level authority:** Souter’s V-A, joined by Stevens, O’Connor, Scalia, Thomas and Breyer; six Justices. The seven-Justice V-B coalition controls removal of (b). All nine accept V-D’s boundaries of the adjudicated issues without opponents thereby joining invalidity of a disputed component.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Section 10(d)’s obscenity exception to access-programming immunity remains and is not general liability for protected indecency. Independent 1996 §506(a) permits refusal on public-access capacity for obscenity, indecency or nudity; its public-access language does not automatically cover all educational/governmental capacity. Section 506(b) separately covers leased access. Neither commands refusal nor imports the 1992 policy/request conditions; their constitutionality and application are not decided or extinguished. Sections 504 and 505 retain their distinct subscriber-request/no-charge and sexually-oriented-channel triggers and transitions; their enactment proves no technical efficacy or actual implementation. Act §561’s three-judge facial-review route is not a new proceeding here. No unconditional carriage right, general private-editor immunity, universal forum designation, damages, new FCC hearing or automatic interim relief follows.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Remand to implement the three distinct component results within the challenged 1992 authorities.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- **ACT/Pacifica (March 4, 1996):** The Court applies its protection of nonobscene indecency and independent necessity/means review to the compulsory (b) arrangement. Its broadcast timetable disposition is not a cable rule. The divided permission opinions preserve the governing protection while disagreeing on application.
- **FCC v. Pacifica Foundation:** Its narrow, contextual broadcast holding remains; it does not automatically sustain every cable indecency restriction or establish that the present protected speech is of lower constitutional value.
- **Sable Communications v. FCC:** The (b) majority applies the distinction between compelling protection of children and adequately justified restrictions on adults. Scalia's separate willing-outlet analysis concerns the permissions and is not the Court's sufficient (b) ground.
- **Turner Broadcasting:** Cable editorial interests retain ordinary speech protection. The prior content-neutral full-power must-carry classification and intermediate standard do not govern an expressly content-selected indecency scheme. Neither the earlier limited shared predictive-review principle nor its fractured record-insufficiency discussion requires remand in every cable case.
- **Hurley:** The protection of an actual private expressive presentation remains intact. The component opinions disagree about the legal consequences of access duties; none establishes that ownership alone makes every independent access program the operator's message.
- **Perry and Cornelius:** Their attention to the actual forum and government's arrangement remains. The Court creates no universal cable-access forum; Kennedy's conditional forum ground does not become such a holding.
- **Rosenberger, Pinette and Chabad:** Their program-specific viewpoint, attribution and contextual rules are not converted into a presumption that every regulated channel is a public forum or governmental speaker. The divided opinions' use of those limits creates no new general forum or attribution test.
- **Blum, Jackson and Lugar; Reitman and Crawford:** The distinction between a private act and governmental alteration or encouragement remains relevant. No categorical operator immunity or rule making every private refusal government action is adopted.
- **Alaska Airlines:** The Court applies independent operation and congressional intent in retaining (a) after invalidating (b).

No earlier decision is overruled. The separate opinions' broader grounds do not independently alter controlling law.

### Commercial speech and alcohol-price advertising

#### 44 Liquormart, Inc. v. Rhode Island, 517 U.S. 484

**Docket or dockets:** No. 94-1140.
**Decided:** May 13, 1996.

##### Material advancement and reasonable fit of truthful-price restrictions

**Holding:** Even under ordinary *Central Hudson* review and treating temperance as substantial, Rhode Island has not demonstrated that these truthful-price restrictions directly and materially reduce consumption. The holding concerns this record and restriction, not every possible effect of advertising, prices, or demand; supported prediction remains permissible without a mandatory state-specific numerical study or experimental certainty.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy's Part I, joined by Stone-Zsela, Stevens, Souter and Ginsburg; five. Stevens affirmatively adopts this independently sufficient conditional application without accepting consumer ignorance as legitimate or ordinary scrutiny as the complete constitutional account.

**Material application:** The State's search-cost/price-dispersion mechanism and opposing experts' concessions of price responsiveness and theoretical plausibility are material but do not overcome the trial finding of no significant consumption effect. General-advertising studies with control problems, missing estimates connecting this restriction's projected price change to consumption, and possible market-share gains without aggregate consumption gains fail to establish material advancement. Constitutional sufficiency is independently assessed without turning appellate economic inference into a new trial finding.

**Independent alternative holding:** Even assuming material advancement, continuously suppressing this category of truthful retail-price information is disproportionate to the temperance objective on this record. Concrete direct price and tax alternatives expose inadequately justified fit; they are neither mandatory replacements nor a least-restrictive-means rule.

**Proposition-level authority for alternative holding:** Kennedy's Part II, joined by Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer; seven. O'Connor and Breyer assume advancement; Souter adopts both failures; Stevens's application remains conditional. Scalia's judgment vote and Thomas's categorical theory supply no additional balancing votes.

**Material application:** Interstate-shopping concerns do not explain why the State's indirect price mechanism avoids the same leakage or justify the informational burden. Section 3-8-7 permits merchandise-attached or merchandise-placed price signs or tags inside licensed premises under departmental rules; Regulation 32 forbids references visible from outside Class A premises. Section 3-8-8.1 separately excepts recognized, authorized trade journals. These exceptions and lawful nonprice promotion neither automatically defeat nor establish fit; the challenged category is complete subject to those exact exceptions, rather than a ban on all alcohol speech.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Ordinary *Central Hudson/Fox* review remains operative. No majority adopts a special-care or heightened-review tier, categorical anti-ignorance rule, universal alternatives checklist, all-sources-at-once requirement, or independent interstate-information immunity. False or misleading speech, unlawful promotions, and direct alcohol controls retain their own governing law; the Court selects no tax or minimum-price program and decides no antitrust dispute.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *Edenfield*, *Ibanez*, *Lanphere*, and *Rubin* require proof responsive to the actual restriction. *Fox* supplies reasonable proportional fit; *Discovery Network* and *Rubin* support concrete comparisons without least-restrictive-means review. *Edge* retains its record-specific meaningful-reduction holding; *Florida Bar*'s invalidation does not prohibit supported prediction. *Midcal* and *324 Liquor* invalidate particular price arrangements, not every state-imposed price control. Subsequent searching scrutiny denies automatic *Posadas* authorization here, but broader repudiation of its paternalism and greater-power reasoning has only four votes. *Queensgate* remains a summary merits disposition confined by *Mandel* to what it necessarily decided, rather than a rule that comparable restrictions invariably survive later developed advancement-and-fit doctrine. *Bigelow* supplies no separate adopted interstate holding.

##### Effect of the Twenty-first Amendment on speech protection

**Holding:** Alcohol-control authority supplies no additional presumption relaxing First Amendment protection for these off-premises truthful-price restrictions. Authority over lawful sales does not itself validate suppression of accurate information, and accepting a license does not surrender speech rights.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy's Part III-A, unanimous; this agreement does not attribute balancing to Scalia or Thomas.

##### The broader speech rule and LaRue's enhanced-deference rationale

**Holding:** The Twenty-first Amendment does not qualify the First Amendment's protection of speech. *LaRue*'s reliance on the Twenty-first Amendment to enhance deference is disavowed; its holding remains supported by ordinary police powers over the regulated conduct.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy's Part III-B, joined by Stevens, Scalia, Souter, Thomas and Ginsburg; six. Stone-Zsela, O'Connor and Breyer do not join this broader rule.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *LaRue*'s identified rationale loses force, but its conduct holding and *Bellanca*'s conduct result remain intact. The broader rule concerns speech protection, not invalidity of every direct alcohol restriction.

##### Operative relief on both preserved speech claims

**Holding:** Reversal requires implementation of the district court's constitutional declaration against the challenged prohibitions in §§3-8-7 and 3-8-8.1 and Regulation 32; the completed record requires no new merits trial. The Court issues no additional injunction directive.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy's Part V-B, joined by all seven other Associates; eight. Reversal on both plaintiffs' First Amendment claims is unanimous; Stone-Zsela would additionally direct a prospective injunction, which is not the mandate.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Reverse the operative October 24 First Circuit judgment and remand to implement the declaration. The paid $400 fine and unappealed administrative order are not reopened; no damages or refund is awarded. Peoples' waived Commerce Clause claim remains outside review. General enforcement authority in §3-8-8 and every other alcohol-advertising rule are not independently invalidated.

### Existing government contractors and retaliatory termination

#### Board of County Commissioners, Wabaunsee County v. Umbehr, 518 U.S. 668 (1996)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 94-1654.
**Decided:** June 28, 1996.

##### Whether an existing independent contractor can challenge speech-retaliatory termination

**Holding:** Government may not terminate or refuse to renew an existing independent-contractor relationship because the contractor spoke as a private citizen on a matter of public concern when the speech and public interests outweigh the government's legitimate contracting and operational interests. Courts apply Pickering's balance to the actual contractual relationship, with appropriate regard for genuine service needs; contractor status, retained termination power and absence of a property entitlement do not by themselves defeat the claim.

**Proposition-level authority:** Souter’s opinion, joined by Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O’Connor, Kennedy, Ginsburg and Breyer; seven Justices.

**Material application:** The County’s existing renewable exclusive arrangement carried valuable benefits despite no direct purchase of hauling. Loss of exclusivity, coordinated negotiation and notice protection can cause injury notwithstanding later direct city contracts. Content, form and context determine public concern. Actual independence, other clients, contacts and responsibilities may affect the balance either way; private communication is not automatically unprotected and offense at criticism is not a service interest.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No initial-bidder, universal future-award, pure affiliation, unrelated employee-status, comprehensive factual-mistake, later-acquired-evidence or mitigation holding. Summary-judgment assumptions establish no actual speech protection, motive, injury or ultimate balance.

##### What causation and same-decision requirements govern the remand

**Holding:** The contractor must establish that protected speech was a substantial or motivating factor in the challenged action. The government may defeat the retaliation claim by proving by a preponderance of the evidence that it would have taken the same action absent the protected speech; identifying a merely possible lawful reason does not establish that defense. Official-capacity liability and relief also require the ordinary entity-attribution and remedial predicates.

**Proposition-level authority:** Souter’s opinion, joined by Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O’Connor, Kennedy, Ginsburg and Breyer; seven Justices.

**Material application:** The claimant’s motivating-factor burden and government’s preponderance counterfactual defense remain separate. Genuine performance, efficiency, cost, trust and operational grounds remain available; their possible existence is not proof. Personal immunity is distinct from official-capacity entity liability.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Waters/Settle do not supply a universal investigation framework. Ordinary Monell attribution and remedy predicates remain necessary.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Reviewed official-capacity judgment affirmed and remanded, 7–2. The individual-immunity judgment and McClure’s separate causation judgment are undisturbed; no automatic renewal, reinstatement, damages or trial.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- **Pickering and Connick:** Extended to existing-contractor retaliation through a balance adjusted to the actual service relationship, preserving private-citizen/public-concern and genuine operational-interest inquiries.
- **Perry v. Sindermann:** Applied to distinguish absence of entitlement to continued benefits from an unconstitutional retaliatory condition.
- **Givhan:** Preserves protection for qualifying citizen expression communicated privately; delivery method alone does not resolve the claim.
- **Mt. Healthy:** Applied without changing the motivating-factor burden or the government's preponderance same-decision defense.
- **Waters and Settle:** Their actual genuine-ground and causation distinctions remain operative; no full investigation framework or unrelated curricular rule is adopted here.
- **National Treasury Employees Union:** Its broad prospective-restraint rule remains distinct from this individual termination; its full justification allocation is not automatically imported.
- **Kentucky v. Graham and Monell:** Preserve the distinction between personal immunity and entity claims and the independent requirements for governmental attribution and relief.

### Political affiliation and recurring service providers

#### O’Hare Truck Service, Inc. v. City of Northlake, 518 U.S. 712 (1996)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 95-191.
**Decided:** June 28, 1996.

##### Whether recurring service referrals may be withdrawn for refusal of political support

**Holding:** Government may not withdraw an existing independent-contractor or regular service-provider relationship because the provider refuses partisan support or supports an opponent, unless the government demonstrates that political affiliation is an appropriate requirement for effective performance of the actual work. That protection reaches the pleaded recurring towing referrals even without a direct municipal purchase, employment relationship or property entitlement.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stevens’s opinion, joined by Stone-Zsela, O’Connor, Kennedy, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer; seven Justices.

**Material application:** Branti’s exception turns on demonstrated function, not contractor, policymaker or confidential-worker labels. Rewarding allies and generalized patronage benefits are insufficient. The pleaded towing function makes no policy, holds no confidential political role and speaks for no administration. Customers’ payment and other business do not eliminate the benefit of controlled referrals.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The Rule 12(b)(6) allegations are accepted only for the motion. No initial-bidder, every-allocation, lesser-referral-reduction, property-entitlement, general employee-status or criminal bribery rule.

##### How affiliation and speech or materially mixed claims remain distinct

**Holding:** The functional affiliation rule does not replace Pickering's analysis of public-concern speech or materially mixed speech-and-affiliation claims. Courts must identify the developed claim and apply the appropriate inquiry: whether political allegiance is genuinely required for the work, or whether protected citizen speech and the public's interests outweigh the government's legitimate service interests in the actual relationship.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stevens’s opinion, joined by Stone-Zsela, O’Connor, Kennedy, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer; seven Justices.

**Material application:** Appropriate allegiance for effective work and actual expression’s effect on service are different questions. Pickering/Connick require the service-adjusted balance and public-concern inquiry where the developed claim calls for them.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No universal affiliation test for speech disputes or imported NTEU prospective-restraint or full Waters factual-error/investigation framework.

##### What causation, defenses and remedy predicates remain

**Holding:** The claimants must establish the relevant protected conduct and show that it was a substantial or motivating factor in the removal. Under Mt. Healthy, the City may prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the same decision would have occurred absent that conduct; a hypothetical permissible reason is insufficient. Governmental attribution, individual defenses and remedies retain their ordinary independent requirements.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stevens’s opinion, joined by Stone-Zsela, O’Connor, Kennedy, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer; seven Justices.

**Material application:** Neutral safety, reliability, responsiveness, economy and integrity grounds remain available on supported facts. Mere possibility of a lawful reason cannot defeat the pleaded causal claim. Municipal attribution, individual defenses and relief require independent proof.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No actual coercion, retaliatory motive, personal or municipal liability, damages or immunity conclusion is established.

**Operative remedy or transition:** First Amendment dismissal reversed and remanded, 7–2. The separate due-process disposition is undisturbed. Ordinary summary judgment remains available on a developed record; no compelled trial, list restoration or permanent referrals.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- **Elrod and Branti:** Their protection against impermissible affiliation conditions is extended to the existing contractor or regular-provider relationship, retaining the government's functional appropriate-affiliation exception.
- **Rutan:** Its employee-benefit extension supports examining the reason for government action rather than confining protection to tenure; it did not itself previously resolve this recurring-provider setting.
- **Perry v. Sindermann:** Applied to distinguish lack of a property entitlement from freedom to impose an unconstitutional condition.
- **Pickering and Connick:** Supply the distinct speech/public-concern inquiry for an appropriately developed speech or mixed claim, adjusted to actual service interests rather than displaced by a universal affiliation test.
- **Mt. Healthy:** Applied without changing the claimant's motivating-factor burden or the City's preponderance same-decision defense.
- **Waters and Settle:** Their genuine-ground and actual-cause distinctions remain in force; no new complete factual-error or investigation framework is adopted.
- **National Treasury Employees Union:** Its advance-restraint rule remains distinct from this individual referral removal.
- **Monell:** Its independent governmental-attribution requirements remain necessary; reversal does not establish municipal liability.

### Political-party campaign expenditures

#### Colorado Republican Federal Campaign Committee v. Federal Election Commission, 518 U.S. 604 (1996)

**Docket or dockets:** No. 95-489.
**Decided:** June 26, 1996.

##### Whether the Senate party-expenditure ceiling may reach this independent advertisement

**Holding:** A political party's own campaign advertisement that is genuinely independent of a candidate may not be subjected to the Senate-election expenditure ceiling in 2 U.S.C. §441a(d)(3) merely because its speaker is an official political party. Party identity and a continuing electoral relationship do not, without more, justify applying that ceiling to this independent expression; the adverse enforcement judgment must therefore be vacated.

**Proposition-level authority:** O’Connor’s Part I, joined by Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas and Breyer; six direct votes.

**Current-force modification:** FEC v. Colorado Republican Federal Campaign Committee, June 25, 2001, resolves the reserved facial coordinated-spending question by sustaining the presented Senate ceiling against categorical party immunity on the developed circumvention record. The government must establish objective circumvention risk and close fit while preserving meaningful association and advocacy. The independent-advertisement judgment and actual candidate-connection requirement remain intact; the new ruling neither validates every coordinated expressive application nor supplies a universal monetary safe harbor.

**Material application:** The party’s $15,000 pre-nomination advertisement was genuinely independent. Its prior assignment of the whole $103,248 adjusted election allowance explains statutory excess, not constitutional validity. Legitimate corruption and circumvention concerns do not establish an actual candidate connection from party identity alone.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No majority adopts the complete narrower expenditure framework or its prudential reservation rationale (O’Connor, Souter, Breyer), or Kennedy/Scalia/Thomas’s broader coordinated-party-expression protection. No Marks combination is used. Coordinated expression, direct candidate cash, earmarks, republication, sham independence and actual conduits are neither generally immunized nor upheld by implication. No universal bribery-proof, express-advocacy formula, constitutional dollar floor, vagueness or administrative-deference rule.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Adverse enforcement/penalty mandate vacated and remanded, 6–3. The broader Senate-election counterclaim receives no majority constitutional determination; no fixed penalty, damages, refund or compelled new factual trial.

**Later-authority backlinks:** FEC v. Colorado Republican Federal Campaign Committee, June 25, 2001 — the facial challenge to the Senate coordinated-party expenditure ceiling.

##### Whether party identity supplies the connection required by the alternative contribution theory

**Holding:** For the government's theory that this advertisement is a contribution under §441a(a)(7)(B)(i), party status alone cannot substitute for expenditure made in cooperation, consultation or concert with, or at the request or suggestion of, a candidate, the candidate's authorized political committees or their agents. On the accepted independence premise, that theory cannot preserve the adverse enforcement judgment under §441a(a)(2).

**Proposition-level authority:** The same six-Justice Part I coalition.

**Material application:** A categorical agency characterization is not a factual finding of consultation; competing assertions about novelty and noncontest establish neither forfeiture nor concession. Transfers among national, State, district, local and subordinate same-party committees are exempt from §441a(a)(1) and (2). Candidate-material dissemination, distribution or republication under (a)(7)(B)(ii), and original-source attribution for earmarked/intermediary contributions under (a)(8), have distinct predicates absent here.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The constitutionality of a transaction with an actual connection, all interactions with (d)(1)’s notwithstanding clause, presidential allowances and other House limits are not decided.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- **Buckley v. Valeo, 424 U.S. 1:** Its distinction between independent expenditures and candidate contributions supplies the present independent-advertisement rule. Its treatment of the party provision's Fifth Amendment challenge did not decide this First Amendment question. The general distinction remains in force.
- **FEC v. National Conservative Political Action Committee, 470 U.S. 480:** Its protection of genuinely independent political advocacy supports the result; it supplies no categorical immunity for actual contribution channels.
- **Day v. Holahan, May 15, 1995:** Its controlling protection of meaningful intermediary association and preservation of realistic conduit regulation inform the required distinction. Its recipient category excluded political-party units, and its responsive-financing judgment had no unified controlling rationale. Neither is converted into an earlier decision of this party-spending question.
- **FEC v. Massachusetts Citizens for Life, Inc., 479 U.S. 238:** Its protection of political expression and its nonprofit setting remain distinct; the Court does not rest today's judgment on a universal express-advocacy formula or extend the nonprofit exception to every entity.

### Student speech and curricular control

#### Settle v. Dickson County School Board

**Docket or dockets:** Sixth Circuit No. 93-6207; no separate Supreme Court docket supplied.
**Decided:** June 25, 1996.

##### What genuine curricular grounds may limit a religious research topic

**Holding:** A teacher may enforce genuine topic-approval, research, source and academic-method requirements reasonably related to legitimate pedagogical concerns, and a student's religious convictions create no exemption from them. But curricular discretion does not make categorical exclusion of an otherwise permissible religious perspective, or a mistaken blanket legal prohibition on academic religious subjects, a legitimate ground merely because it is described as educational judgment.

**Proposition-level authority:** Souter’s Part I, unanimous.

**Material application:** The teacher-only submission is not presumed publicly attributable to the school or an open forum. Objective inquiry may be distinguished from devotion or personal testimony. Genuine factual or evaluative mistakes can remain pedagogical judgments, while a legally impermissible categorical religious ban does not become valid as an honest academic mistake. The full policy permits objective, respectful, balanced academic religious treatment without promoting tenets or demeaning belief and accommodates student-initiated belief or nonbelief; neither provision guarantees approval.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No universal curricular viewpoint neutrality, unrestricted topic choice, religion-based exemption, perfect-accuracy duty or independent Free Exercise, Establishment or equal-protection holding.

##### Whether the summary-judgment record establishes lawful cause or the same-decision defense

**Holding:** Summary judgment cannot rest on a merely possible pedagogical justification when supported evidence permits a material inference that a student's work was rejected for an impermissible religious reason rather than legitimate application of assignment requirements. Under Mt. Healthy, the student must establish protected conduct and its substantial or motivating role; defendants may then prove by a preponderance that the same adverse decision would have occurred without that conduct.

**Proposition-level authority:** Souter’s Part II, unanimous.

**Material application:** Failure to secure permission was supported but its independent causal effect was disputed by the next-day no-penalty alternative, mixed reasons and original-choice answer, which also covered Buddha and Muhammed. Faith alone does not prove inability to research. Familiarity does not prove absence of new inquiry. Source requirements must reflect permitted secondary and outside sources, not a new Bible-only or school-library-only premise. Comparator descriptions are relevant without proving identical circumstances.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No pretext, hostility, final causation, liability or automatic defeat of a proved same-decision defense is found. Waters supplies its shared genuine-ground distinction, not an imported employment investigation code. Graduation proves no universal mootness; actual capacities, municipal attribution, immunity and remedies remain open. Conduct-date immunity notice concerns March–April 1991, not later decisions.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Vacated and remanded, 9–0, for ordinary proceedings on the free-speech claim. No compulsory approval, reading, grading, credit, removal of the zero, damages, new discovery procedure or trial; another supported lawful disposition remains possible.

**Treatment of earlier authority:**

- **Hazelwood School District v. Kuhlmeier, 484 U.S. 260:** Applies legitimate pedagogical control to this graded research assignment, preserving genuine method and quality decisions and reasonable academic error. Its public-attribution rationale is not automatically transferred to a teacher-only submission.
- **Tinker v. Des Moines Independent Community School District, 393 U.S. 503:** Preserves student expression without creating unrestricted topic choice or displacing genuine assignment requirements.
- **Epperson v. Arkansas, 393 U.S. 97:** Applies the distinction between curricular authority and constitutional immunity, and between objective academic study of religion and governmental religious instruction. No new religion-clause claim is adjudicated.
- **Lamb's Chapel v. Center Moriches Union Free School District, June 7, 1993; Rosenberger v. Rector and Visitors of the University of Virginia, June 29, 1995; and Good News/Good Sports Club v. School District of Ladue, December 11, 1995:** Preserve the distinction between genuine program boundaries and religious-viewpoint exclusion in their actual settings. They do not classify this assignment as a forum or establish a right to a particular grade.
- **Lee v. Weisman, June 24, 1992, and Sherman v. Community Consolidated School District 21, February 12, 1996:** Preserve their limits on official worship and coercive religious participation without creating a blanket prohibition on academic religious subjects.
- **Waters v. Churchill, May 31, 1994:** Applies the genuine-reliance and causation distinction at its shared scope. Its separate investigation approaches and public-employment balance are not adopted as a classroom test.
- **Mt. Healthy City School District Board of Education v. Doyle, 429 U.S. 274:** Applies the claimant's protected-conduct and substantial-or-motivating-factor burden and defendants' separate preponderance same-decision defense. A possible lawful reason is not sufficient proof, and partial improper motivation does not automatically establish entitlement to relief.

No precedent is overruled.

### Religion-specific public-workplace restrictions

#### Brown v. Polk County

**Docket or dockets:** Eighth Circuit No. 93-3313.
**Decided:** March 17, 1997.

##### Whether operational and Establishment concerns justify these religion-specific directives

**Holding:** A public employer may control work, resources, coercion and official religious activity, but discriminatory commands reaching private religious expression or possession must satisfy the constitutional justification and tailoring their religious targeting requires. The blanket command against witnessing, proselytizing and counseling and the removal of all religious items, including a private desk Bible, exceed the concerns demonstrated here.

**Proposition-level authority:** Opinion of the Court (Stevens), Part I, unanimous.

**Material application:** Preventing official worship, supervisory pressure, favoritism and diversion of paid resources can supply legitimate and potentially compelling interests. Those interests do not justify suppression of all expression in religious terms or personal possession without an established operational effect.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Voluntary, irregular supervisor-led prayer is not automatically private or free of coercion. The Court recognizes no general entitlement to worship in departmental meetings, workplace forum, new equality tier or constitutional discharge claim. The free-exercise ground suffices, and a Title VII violation is not automatically a First Amendment violation.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Smith preserves neutral work rules; Lukumi requires justification and tailoring for religious targeting. Pickering, Connick and Givhan retain their actual employee-speech inquiries. NTEU concerns the protected-citizen reach of broad burdens; Waters does not authorize blanket religious suppression. Pinette supplies no comprehensive majority Establishment test, and Chabad and Good News do not create an office forum.

##### What relief remains for the two actually argued constitutional restrictions

**Holding:** The constitutional remand concerns declaratory or compensatory relief for the reprimand and removal directives, each subject to its own lawful predicates. Constitutional discharge, backpay and reinstatement theories are not added where they were not actually argued, and statutory liability does not establish every constitutional remedy.

**Proposition-level authority:** Opinion of the Court (Stevens), Part IV, unanimous.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Compensation requires injury, causation and defendant-specific responsibility, capacity and municipal attribution; any properly preserved individual immunity remains distinct without reopening settled invalidity. Declaration requires a continuing controversy. No independent constitutional injunction request or independent Iowa-law construction is established.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The reviewed constitutional reversal is affirmed with its appropriate-relief remand. No fixed award, new liability against every defendant or new constitutional termination judgment is entered.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Landgraf and Rivers leave independently available §1983 compensation intact. Arizonans does not make these existing compensation claims automatically moot; Nabozny preserves individual and municipal responsibility, conduct-time notice and remedy distinctions without reopening a completed trial.

For the distinct statutory accommodation, pre-1991 mixed-motive and employment-relief holdings in Brown v. Polk County, Eighth Circuit No. 93-3313, decided March 17, 1997, see Labor and Employment, “Religious accommodation and completed mixed-motive proof.”

### Religious exercise and optional school programs

#### Elizabeth G. Curtis v. School Committee of Falmouth

**Docket or dockets:** Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court review; historical petition No. 95-617.
**Decided:** January 21, 1997.

For the separate questions in Elizabeth G. Curtis v. School Committee of Falmouth, Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court review; historical petition No. 95-617 decided January 21, 1997, see Civil Rights — Parental liberty and optional school programs (The optional program does not establish the claimed parental-liberty infringement).

##### The stated program imposes no established constitutional burden on religious exercise

**Holding:** A program that students may decline without sacrificing ordinary education or another benefit, and that requires neither religiously prohibited participation nor assent, does not burden these families' free exercise merely by making the described condoms available contrary to their religious teaching. The stated program establishes no religious targeting, unequal treatment, penalty for religious refusal, or comparable official pressure to participate.

**Proposition-level authority:** Opinion of the Court (Souter), unanimous.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The case fails at the constitutional burden threshold, so Smith supplies no independent holding and combined parental/free-exercise pleading does not automatically invoke strict scrutiny. Actual religious targeting, official pressure, compulsory participation or benefit penalties remain outside this result. RFRA and unpresented state constitutional or statutory claims are not decided.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The constitutional free-exercise claim requires neither parental exclusion nor notification; summary judgment stands without an injunction or evidentiary remand.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Lyng and Bowen v. Roy distinguish conflict with governmental activity from interference with religious exercise. Lee's official-pressure protection remains; formal voluntariness is not universally dispositive. Lukumi and Settle retain targeting and exclusion protections. Church of Scientology, Swanner and American Life League retain their separate application-specific RFRA inquiries.

### Cable carriage and editorial discretion

#### Turner Broadcasting System, Inc. v. Federal Communications Commission

**Docket or dockets:** No. 95-992.
**Decided:** March 31, 1997.

For the separate classification questions excluded from review, see *Turner*, March 31, 1997, No. 95-992 (Federal Courts — Preservation and question-presented limits).

##### Whether the developed record establishes material advancement of preservation and diversity

**Holding:** On the developed record, the general full-power must-carry scheme materially advances the substantial interests in preserving free local broadcasts and independently available information sources. Supported preventive judgments do not require proof of impending industry collapse or individual failure of every carried station, but remain subject to independent judicial review.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy's Opinion of the Court, Part II, joined by Stone-Zsela, Stevens, Souter, and Breyer; five direct votes support the shared preservation-and-diversity rationale.

**Material application:** Evidence connects bottleneck control and incentives favoring affiliated programming or advertising with carriage refusals, drops, repositioning, lost audience and revenue, and threatened local service. Contrary profitability and growth evidence does not refute every supported local threat. Audience options may be reduced without predatory intent.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The Court adopts no independently sufficient economic-predation or fair-competition application. Legislative prediction is not conclusive, and a desirable broadcast policy alone is insufficient.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *Turner* (1994) supplies the full-power content-neutral classification, intermediate standard, and limited predictive-deference proposition. Its earlier four-Justice account of record insufficiency does not become majority law. *Denver Area* preserves ordinary cable speech protection and separate component review; spectrum-scarcity doctrine is not extended to cable.

##### Whether the existing duties adequately fit the accepted interests on this facial record

**Holding:** The reviewed full-power duties burden no substantially greater amount of cable editorial discretion than necessary to protect the accepted interests on this developed facial record. Intermediate scrutiny requires an adequate fit, not the least restrictive imaginable arrangement; the supported predictive inquiry permits final affirmance without further trial here.

**Proposition-level authority:** Kennedy's Opinion of the Court, Part III, joined by Stone-Zsela, Stevens, Souter, and Breyer; five Justices. O'Connor, Scalia, Thomas, and Ginsburg dissent from the merits affirmance.

**Material application:** Capacity categories, qualified-station and nonduplication rules, and the distinct educational obligations limit the duties. Voluntary carriage counts toward them without eliminating the burden of losing the freedom to change programming. The 1.2 percent figure measures added must-carry channels, not all reserved capacity, displaced programs, or foregone choices. Existing editorial space and expansion matter alongside burdens on operators, programmers, and viewers. The record supports the lower court's conclusion that leased access, A/B switches, narrower former FCC-style rules, and subsidies would not protect the accepted interests as effectively.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Under 47 U.S.C.§534, systems with 12 or fewer usable activated channels must carry at least three local commercial signals; systems also having 300 or fewer subscribers are exempt from that section only while they delete no broadcast signal. Systems with more than 12 channels carry eligible local commercial signals up to one-third of usable activated capacity. This is not a combined commercial-and-educational ceiling. Substantially duplicative commercial signals already represented in carriage and additional same-network affiliates need not be carried; voluntary duplicates and multiple affiliates count toward the obligation. When eligible stations exceed the required number, the operator selects among them, but cannot substitute low power for full power and must choose the elected network's affiliate with the closest city-of-license reference point to the principal headend.

Section535 adds separate educational duties. Systems with 12 or fewer channels carry one qualified local educational signal and may carry more. Systems with 13–36 carry at least one and need not carry more than three, subject to continued carriage; they may carry more. If no qualified local station is present, the former category must import one qualified educational signal and the latter at least one. For that importation, the smallest systems need not remove programming actually provided on March 29, 1990 but must use the first available channel. All qualified local educational stations carried on that date retain carriage unless operator and station give written waiver consent. Systems above36 channels, including those expanding beyond36, carry requesting qualified local educational stations; a system required to carry three need not add stations substantially duplicating another qualified local educational station requesting carriage. This is not a general three-station cap. A13–36-channel system already carrying a State-network educational affiliate need not add another same-network affiliate whose programming substantially duplicates the carried affiliate.

Commercial distant signals require indemnification of increased copyright liability. A commercial station below the specified headend levels (−45dBm UHF; −49dBm VHF) is excluded if it does not agree to bear the costs of delivering a good-quality or baseband signal. Educational carriage is not required without delivery of a good-quality or baseband signal; its distant-signal indemnity exception concerns adding a signal and expressly does not erase the continued-carriage rule. These are actual programming obligations, including primary video, audio and captions. Commercial carriage includes technically feasible program-related blanking-interval or subcarrier material; educational carriage includes technically feasible program-related ancillary material necessary for disability access, education or language purposes. Other ancillary material remains discretionary. Positioning and availability duties also constrain operation; the law does not merely reserve empty channels. No new dispute over ancillary material, positioning, payment, notice or enforcement is decided.

No blanket exemption of legislative facts from summary-judgment rules follows. More burdensome future legislation and supported system-specific displacement challenges remain open. The commercial one-third cap does not combine commercial and educational duties; the educational scheme creates no universal three-station ceiling. No dispute over ancillary programming, positioning, payment, notice, or enforcement is decided.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Affirm the reviewed full-power facial judgment, leaving its duties enforceable. No replacement quota, Act-wide injunction, damages, takings disposition, or religious-claim disposition issues. The separate low-power and market-modification classifications remain outside the judgment.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *O'Brien* requires a substantial nonsuppressive interest and fitted burden. *Ward* requires adequate tailoring while preserving concrete alternatives as relevant evidence, without a least-restrictive-means command.

### Electronic obscenity distribution

#### United States v. Thomas

**Docket or dockets:** Sixth Circuit Nos. 94-6648 and 94-6649; no separate Supreme Court docket assigned.
**Decided:** 1997-05-19.

For offense-date statutory coverage and continuing-offense venue, see Criminal Procedure — Electronic obscenity transportation and venue, United States v. Thomas, May 19, 1997, these dockets.

##### Receiving-community standards apply to this controlled distribution

**Holding:** When operators screen and approve a subscriber, know his receiving community and knowingly authorize delivery there, Miller's geographic community standards may govern prurient appeal and patent offensiveness. Serious literary, artistic, political or scientific value remains Pope's reasonable-person inquiry, independent of local approval; no national cyberspace standard is required on this record.

**Proposition-level authority:** Ginsburg's Part II, joined by Stone-Zsela, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas and Breyer; eight direct joins. Stevens does not join.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The operators screened membership, knew the Memphis destination and authorized delivery by password. Open websites, anonymous networks, unavoidable routing and publishers unable to identify or control recipients are reserved. Factual knowledge differs from knowledge of obscenity law or ultimate legal classification; a willing recipient does not exempt otherwise unprotected obscenity.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Miller and Hamling supply receiving-community standards for prurient appeal and patent offensiveness; Pope preserves objective serious-value review. Sable applies obscenity doctrine to controlled electronic transmission while preserving protected indecency. X-Citement Video retains its statute-specific factual-knowledge distinction.

### Military statements as relevant evidence

#### Thomasson v. Perry

**Docket or dockets:** Fourth Circuit No. 95-2185; review of 80 F.3d 915 (en banc).

**Decided:** 1997-06-09.

For the equal-protection question and statutory qualifications in Thomasson v. Perry, Fourth Circuit No. 95-2185, decided June 9, 1997, see Civil Rights — Military personnel and equal protection.

##### Relevant evidentiary use of this voluntary statement does not violate the First Amendment

**Holding:** The First Amendment does not prohibit using Thomasson's voluntary identity statement as relevant evidence of the lawful conduct-related personnel predicate sustained in Part I, with the genuine rebuttal opportunity present here. That evidentiary use does not authorize discharge merely for opposing the policy, punish abstract belief, or make every identity statement an admission of a prohibited act.

**Proposition-level authority:** O'Connor's opinion, joined by Scalia, Kennedy, Thomas and Breyer; five direct joins.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The relevant connection rests on the lawful conduct-related inference and meaningful rebuttal sustained in Part I. A bare evidentiary label cannot justify punishment of expression. Advocacy retaliation, an irrelevant inference and abstract belief remain outside the holding. Neither a completed prohibited act nor realized operational disruption is required for this bounded predictive use.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Reject the independent speech challenge by five direct joins. Stevens would independently reverse on speech; Stone-Zsela, Souter and Ginsburg reserve that question and supply no additional support for rejecting it.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Dawson forbids punishment of irrelevant abstract beliefs; Mitchell permits relevant expression as evidence without importing its criminal predicates into every personnel case. Waters preserves scrutiny of the ground actually relied on without adding a universal investigation checklist or actual-disruption condition.

### Official municipal religious identification

#### Robinson v. City of Edmond

**Docket or dockets:** Tenth Circuit Nos. 94-6237 and 95-6008; 68 F.3d 1226 identifies the judgment below.
**Decided:** March 31, 1997.

For recurring-contact standing, see *Robinson*, March 31, 1997, Nos. 94-6237 and 95-6008 (Federal Courts — Standing and personal injury).

##### Whether a privately designed but officially adopted civic seal is municipal expression

**Holding:** A municipality's selection and adoption of an official seal used to authenticate its communications, personnel, and property makes the seal its own expression, despite private origin. Attribution does not by itself make every governmental religious acknowledgment unconstitutional.

**Proposition-level authority:** Breyer's Opinion of the Court, Part II, unanimous.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *Pinette* and *Chabad-Lubavitch of Vermont v. Burlington* preserve neutral private access but distinguish official adoption. *Rosenberger*'s protection of independently edited private expression does not convert the City's identifier into private speech.

##### Whether this continuing civic identifier establishes an impermissible religious affiliation

**Holding:** Government violates the Establishment Clause when the full context of its continuing civic expression identifies it with a particular faith. An assumed secular historical purpose and accompanying secular images do not necessarily cure that effect.

**Proposition-level authority:** Part III, joined by Breyer, Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Souter, and Ginsburg; six Justices.

**Material application:** The recognizable Christian cross occupies an identifying quadrant in the composite seal used across official municipal operations. The design, history, uses, and lack of church control are considered together; favorable reactions and age do not settle the constitutional inquiry.

**Independent alternative holding:** A city may not deliberately and pervasively make a recognizable faith symbol a permanent identifying element of its present civil authority. Edmond's actual combination of official adoption, institutional-identification function, and continuing use independently violates that rule.

**Proposition-level authority for alternative holding:** Part IV, unanimous. The Court directly adopts the bounded distinction from Kennedy's *Allegheny* separate writing; nine direct votes, rather than a combination of incompatible rationales, establish its authority here.

**Limits, remedy, transition, or precedent treatment:** The alternative requires the actual institutional-use combination, not merely governmental ownership or religious subject matter. It requires no proven evangelical motive, church control, added proselytizing inscription, compelled profession, denied benefit, or visual dominance. Religious place names, historical buildings, inherited coats of arms, holiday acknowledgments, exhibits, and private symbols retain their separate contexts; none is categorically approved or invalidated.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The effects ground demands neither an offense poll nor coercion and creates no context-free graphic prohibition. Purpose and entanglement need not be independently decided. No new credibility finding or universal constitutional-fact review rule is adopted.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *Lemon* supplies the independent effects inquiry without being replaced. *Allegheny* supplies contextual affiliation analysis and the distinction adopted in the alternative holding. *Lee*'s school grounds remain distinct; coercion is not the exclusive municipal-seal inquiry. *Kiryas Joel*'s denominational civil-authority rule is not enlarged into a universal display prohibition.

**Current-force modification:** Effective June 23, 1997, Lemon remains the governing Establishment Clause test as modified in Agostini v. Felton, Holding I. Purpose, effects and entanglement inform a single inquiry with three routes: controlling specific prohibition or distinct doctrine, established permissible relationship, and residual attribution and function. Clear cases apply that test; its former independent prongs do not remain a separate or fallback method.

**Later-authority backlinks:** Agostini v. Felton; Chancellor, Board of Education of the City of New York v. Felton, Nos. 96-552 and 96-553, June 23, 1997, Holdings I–II; First Amendment — Public instruction on religious-school premises.

##### What prospective relief follows from unconstitutional present official use

**Holding:** Relief must end use of the cross-bearing seal as the City's current official identifier within a reasonable implementation period set by the District Court, while permitting accurate contextual preservation of historical records and displays.

**Proposition-level authority:** Part V, unanimous.

**Operative remedy or transition:** The granted Establishment Clause judgment is affirmed. The Court prescribes no replacement design, destruction of artifacts, suppression of private speech, or fixed deadline. Longevity does not justify indefinite continuing official use.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Personal liability, immunity, nominal damages, unappealed Free Exercise and state-law claims, attorney-client production, and independent fees or costs are outside this merits determination. Existing proper relief and fee proceedings are not displaced, but no new fee award is made.

### Official school worship and private student expression

#### Ingebretsen v. Jackson Public School District

**Docket or dockets:** Fifth Circuit No. 94-60631; 88 F.3d 274 identifies the judgment below.
**Decided:** March 19, 1997.

For personal standing and both intervention rulings, see *Ingebretsen*, March 19, 1997, No. 94-60631 (Federal Courts — Standing and intervention in school-religion litigation).

##### Whether student delivery or a disclaimer insulates officially organized school worship

**Holding:** The Establishment Clause forbids a school's organization, adoption, direction, or religious supervision of worship within its own event. Student initiation or delivery and a statutory disclaimer do not alone make that activity private, and official sponsorship can violate the Clause without a separate quantified-pressure showing.

**Proposition-level authority:** Ginsburg's Opinion of the Court, Part II, joined by Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Souter, and Breyer; six Justices directly adopt the sponsorship ground.

**Material application:** Section 1(2)'s permission for student-initiated, nonsectarian, nonproselytizing prayer at compulsory and noncompulsory events cannot be administered through official devotional organization or religious supervision. Section 1(4)'s disclaimer cannot erase actual official conduct. Section 2's prohibition on prescribing prayer's form or content is a legal command, not a finding that officials always obey or violate it.

**Independent alternative holding:** School direction of religious exercise also violates the Clause when compulsory attendance or comparable practical pressures create actual pressure to participate. Calling participation voluntary or using a student speaker does not eliminate that inquiry; offense at another student's private viewpoint is insufficient.

**Proposition-level authority for alternative holding:** Part III, joined by Ginsburg, Stevens, O'Connor, Kennedy, Souter, and Breyer; six direct votes independently support this ground, without a *Marks* synthesis.

**Limits, remedy, transition, or precedent treatment:** *Lee* supplies the separate sponsorship and school-pressure rules. Pressure requires no quantified measurement or legal penalty, but is not presumed from hearing private religious speech or attending any voluntary gathering. The hearing-supported threat justifies bounded interim protection, not final invalidation of every statutory application.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *Pinette* and *Chabad of Southern Ohio* require contextual attribution; a disclaimer or forum label is not conclusive. *Rosenberger* preserves neutral aid to independently edited private speech. *Lamb's Chapel*, *Good News Club*, and *Brown v. Polk County* preserve independent expression without making every school event a private forum or importing employment burdens.

##### Whether the preliminary injunction may exempt graduation categorically or suppress independently lawful expression

**Holding:** Interim relief must address the supported unlawful official mechanism while preserving genuinely private religious expression and independently lawful provisions. Graduation has no automatic student-initiation or student-delivery exception to the official-attribution and pressure inquiries.

**Proposition-level authority:** Part IV's private-expression and lawful-provision limit has all nine joins. Continued restraint, removal of the graduation exemption, and remand are adopted by Ginsburg, Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Kennedy, Souter, and Breyer; Scalia and Thomas would also vacate the retained restraint.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Affirm the supported restraint, vacate the graduation safe harbor and overbroad reach, and remand for a severed, provision- and event-sensitive interim order. Give effect separately to §1(3)'s other voluntary expression, §2's voluntary-prayer provision and prohibition on prescribing content, and §1(5)'s severability direction.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No new forum or wider access entitlement is created by judicial deletion of the religious filters. State-law construction and precise decree terms remain below; no final damages claim or universal statutory invalidity is decided.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** *Lee* forecloses the lower-court *Jones II* criteria as a categorical graduation safe harbor while leaving genuine private graduation speech protected.

### Religious access to private adult programs

#### Church on the Rock v. City of Albuquerque

**Docket or dockets:** Tenth Circuit No. 95-2009; no separate Supreme Court docket assigned.
**Decided:** 1997-05-27.

##### Religious advocacy is a viewpoint within this admitted program

**Holding:** A city that permits private movies and instruction on religion, morality, history, literature and philosophy may not exclude an otherwise eligible presentation because it affirmatively teaches a faith, invites conversion or prayer, or offers religious literature. This rule governs the film and literature within this actual senior-center program, while preserving genuine, reasonable and viewpoint-neutral subject and activity limits.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stone-Zsela's opinion, unanimous in Parts I, II and IV.

**Limits and questions not reached:** This admitted film-and-literature activity does not erase every worship/discussion distinction in every limited forum.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Lamb's Chapel and Good News/Good Sports distinguish religious viewpoints on admitted subjects from genuine activity exclusions; standalone worship reservations remain.

##### This private access does not establish religion

**Holding:** Allowing the requested privately sponsored presentation on the actual voluntary, nonresidential adult-program terms does not violate the Establishment Clause. Public ownership and devotional content do not alone convert the speaker's expression into governmental worship; actual official selection, control, adoption, preference or obscured sponsorship could produce a different case.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stone-Zsela's opinion, unanimous in Parts I, II and IV.

**Limits and questions not reached:** Voluntary attendance alone does not cure official worship or institutional identification; forum labels and hypothetical disclaimers establish no categorical immunity.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Lamb's Chapel and Good News preserve actual private access; Lee and Ingebretsen concern official organization/pressure, and Robinson concerns the government's own identification.

##### Context satisfies the retained purpose, effect and entanglement inquiry

**Holding:** Under Lemon, equal private access here serves the secular purpose of the City's broad activity forum, does not primarily advance religion as governmental expression, and creates no excessive entanglement. Actual private attribution and the program's operation, considered together, establish that conclusion without a universal disclaimer, monitoring duty or devotional-financing entitlement.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stone-Zsela's Part III, joined by Stevens, O'Connor, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer; six direct joins. Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas do not join the complete methodology.

**Limits and questions not reached:** A neutral identification notice is available but is no condition of the injunction. No universal disclaimer, devotional-monitoring duty or compulsory financing right follows.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Lemon retains purpose, primary effect and entanglement. Good News and Chabad require real private-attribution examination; Pinette supplies no universal forum immunity. Rosenberger's bounded printing benefit creates no general devotional-funding entitlement.

**Current-force modification:** Effective June 23, 1997, Lemon remains the governing Establishment Clause test as modified in Agostini v. Felton, Holding I. Purpose, effects and entanglement inform a single inquiry with three routes: controlling specific prohibition or distinct doctrine, established permissible relationship, and residual attribution and function. Clear cases apply that test; its former independent prongs do not remain a separate or fallback method.

**Later-authority backlinks:** Agostini v. Felton; Chancellor, Board of Education of the City of New York v. Felton, Nos. 96-552 and 96-553, June 23, 1997, Holdings I–II; First Amendment — Public instruction on religious-school premises.

##### The funding defense does not defeat bounded as-applied relief

**Holding:** The invoked Older Americans Act funding condition does not justify this unconstitutional denial of equal private access. The as-applied injunction and appellate fee entitlement are affirmed, with fee amount left below and ordinary neutral facility administration preserved.

**Proposition-level authority:** Stone-Zsela's opinion, unanimous in Parts I, II and IV.

**Operative remedy or transition:** Affirm reversal of City summary judgment, the as-applied film/literature injunction and appellate fee entitlement, leaving reasonable fee amount below. Neutral scheduling, eligibility, safety, capacity, identification and genuine prospective viewpoint-neutral forum definitions remain available.

**Limits and questions not reached:** No facial Older Americans Act ruling, general grant-administration ruling, damages, fixed fees, withdrawal of funds or relief against the United States is entered.

### Public instruction on religious-school premises

#### Agostini v. Felton; Chancellor, Board of Education of the City of New York v. Felton

**Docket or dockets:** Nos. 96-552 and 96-553.
**Decided:** June 23, 1997.

**Material judgment:** Both judgments vacated and remanded, 5–4, for tailored prospective Rule 60(b)(5) relief; Lemon modified as the governing test; Aguilar's categorical rule overruled and Ball's corresponding Shared Time rationale displaced at the stated scope.

**Proposition-level authority:** All four holdings are delivered by Chief Justice Stone-Zsela in the Opinion of the Court, joined in full by Justices O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas. Each has five direct joins at its stated level of generality, including the modification of Lemon in Holding I. No aggregation of separate opinions supplies controlling authority.

##### I. Lemon governs through one inquiry into governmental religious authority and function

**Holding:** Lemon remains the governing Establishment Clause test, modified so that purpose, effects and entanglement are evidence within one inquiry: a specific prohibition or distinct doctrine controls when it resolves the conduct; an established permissible relationship defeats the claim on that ground; otherwise a legally sufficient unresolved allegation is decided through attribution and function under ordinary procedure. These are three routes within the updated Lemon test, not freestanding prongs, exemptions from review or an alternative test for uncertain cases.

**Proposition-level authority:** Part I of the Opinion of the Court; Chief Justice Stone-Zsela and Justices O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas join this modification in full, supplying five direct joins at this level of generality.

**Operative qualifications:** The court identifies the governmental act—an official message, organized event, exercise of supervisory power or expenditure—and the function it performs. For financing, the question is what government purchases or performs; all religious conduct of the recipient need not become government speech. Private-access authorization, religious identity and physical location are relevant in context but are not individually decisive.

Government may not organize worship as its own activity, prescribe religious profession or observance, adopt doctrine as governmental truth, solicit religious adherence through public authority, govern theology or confer civil authority on a religious basis. Denominational classifications retain their distinct strict-scrutiny rule. Independently identifiable secular work in a religious setting may be purchased with enforceable controls against devotional use and diversion. Restoration of private exercise restricted by custody or comparable governmental control remains subject to the applicable accommodation inquiry, not an automatic financing prohibition. Those distinct doctrines retain their own sources and burdens.

**Controlling explanation:** Lemon addresses governmental sponsorship of religion, financing of religious functions and the improper union of civil and religious authority. Its method must identify those acts rather than condemn an independently secular service because officials supervise it to remain secular. Aguilar exposes that defect: location and repeated contact become substitutes for examining what the public program actually does. The Court therefore modifies Lemon's operation while retaining its constitutional concerns.

Purpose and effects help identify the governmental function; institutional relationships show who directs it. Once prohibited conduct is established, actual conversion, religious success or a completed penalty is unnecessary. A secular objective cannot justify prohibited religious means. Conversely, a provider's religious motivation does not make its secular work devotional. Ordinary monitoring of secular performance is not itself establishment, even when repeated; civil control of doctrine and religious control of public authority remain forbidden.

This method requires real operational separation and reliable accountability for funded work, but not invariably separate institutional governance or wholly distinct personnel. Shared structures cannot excuse devotional financing, and they do not automatically defeat a genuinely severable public service. Here public selection, staffing, materials and supervision identify the remedial service to be examined. The school's entire religious mission is not the governmental act.

The dissent's institutional-support objection warrants scrutiny of the service, not a presumption that its secular and religious functions are inseparable. Existing specific holdings continue to govern their established relationships: Kiryas Joel restricts denominational allocation of civil power; Rosenberger permits its controlled publication benefit; Pinette and Chabad distinguish private expression and governmental attribution. The Court does not decide absent voucher, monument, legislative-prayer or accommodation programs, or declare every future application compatible with every preserved precedent.

**Limits and questions not reached:** The Court decides no tuition-voucher or provider-redemption scheme, monument, legislative-prayer program, general accommodation rule or all forms of direct aid. Parental selection does not itself answer what a particular expenditure purchases; no conclusion about an absent program displaces Witters or Mueller. Religious editorial viewpoint in Rosenberger is not automatically purchased devotional instruction. Private speech, free exercise, institutional religious autonomy, denominational scrutiny and accommodation retain their distinct sources and burdens. No controlling rationale is drawn from separate opinions under Marks.

**Treatment of earlier authority:** Lemon v. Kurtzman remains governing, with its independent purpose, primary-effect and excessive-entanglement prongs modified into the three routes of this single inquiry. The actual holdings of Kiryas Joel, Rosenberger, Pinette, Chabad, Witters and Mueller remain in force; Zobrest supplies no Establishment Clause merits holding. Kiryas Joel's denominational-allocation and accommodation holdings remain intact; its preservation of Aguilar and Ball established the rule entering this decision, not a bar to the Court's express overruling. Zobrest's antecedent-law remand remains; it supplied no Establishment Clause merits holding and did not already undermine Aguilar by such a holding. Rosenberger's actual controlled vendor-funded printing benefit remains permissible on its program terms; it concerns financing, not merely facility access, and neither decided this public-teaching case nor authorized every devotional expenditure.
